title: Oncall slab-to-commit switchback proforma
summary: Compact scenario proforma modeling switching between slab (on-demand/on-call) coverage and committed capacity. Maps price corridors to hiring triggers and quantifies 3 sensitivity cases including a sudden demand kicker.
content:
Objective:
This sheet explores a hybrid operational playbook where we maintain an oncall slab pool for short bursts and a committed capacity ladder for predictable base load. The model tests when to 'switchback' (move from slab-heavy to commit-heavy posture) given price compression or demand spikes, and what headcount/hiring cadence that implies for infra ops and SRE oncall rotations.

Context / why this matters:
- Slab/oncall is cheap to stand up but exposes us to variable unit cost and SRE burn.
- Committed buys lower per-token cost but increases fixed spend and requires headcount commitments (ops/infra rostering, longer-term hiring).
- Customers and enterprise contracts may require low-latency reserved capacity; switching too late costs SLA breaches, switching too early wastes cash.

Key assumptions (editable inputs):
- Baseline monthly token volume (hosted API): 120B tokens/month.
- Slab marginal cost (avg): $0.000025 / token (includes burst premium + oncall overtime buffer).
- Committed marginal cost (avg at 70% utilization): $0.000016 / token (reflects reserved GPU discounts + improved batching).
- Committed fixed monthly cost tiers: small: $60k, medium: $180k, large: $420k (maps to GPU pools and reserved contracts).
- Hiring cadence: new infra SRE hire fully productive for capacity ops in 10 weeks; cost (loaded) $18k/mo after ramp.
- Oncall coverage: 1 oncall per 40k tokens/sec sustained equivalent; scaling headcount needed when sustained 7d rolling average > 80% of slab pool.
- Demand kicker scenario: sudden sustained +50% volume for 6 weeks followed by reversion to baseline.
- Price compression scenario: slab price falls by 20% (market competition) making slab more attractive but transient.

Inputs matrix (quick reference):
- Baseline volume: 120B /mo
- Demand kicker volume: 180B /mo for 6 weeks
- Slab cost per token: $0.000025 baseline; $0.000020 post-compression
- Commit cost per token: $0.000016 (constant)
- Commit ladder sizes (tokens/mo capacity at 75% util): small 60B, medium 180B, large 420B

Scenarios run (automated in the sheet):
1) Baseline (no kicker, no price change)
   - Recommended posture: small commit to cover base 60B (50%), keep remainder on slab.
   - Monthly cost: commit fixed + commit tokens + slab tokens
     * Fixed: $60k
     * Commit token effective marginal: 60B * $0.000016 = $960k
     * Slab token: 60B * $0.000025 = $1.5M
     * Total proforma cost: $2.52M /mo
   - Ops headcount: 2 infra ops (covering commit lifecycle), 3 oncall rotations for slab coverage; hiring not triggered.

2) Demand kicker (+50% for 6w then reversion)
   - Reaction window: can absorb first 2 weeks on slab above baseline (burst).
   - At week 3 sustained above 140B/mo equivalent, trigger medium commit spin-up (procurement + infra config).
   - Procurement lead time: 3 weeks -> commit comes online at week 6 of kicker (near tail).
   - Cost math (6-week window approximation):
     * Extra slab spend for burst weeks 1-2: delta 60B at slab cost -> 60B * $0.000025 * (2/4.3) ~ $0.7M (pro rata for weeks)
     * Commit ramp cost (pro-rated fixed + tokens while spinning up): medium fixed $180k for one month fraction + medium token billing for overlapped period -> net savings small; but commit reduces slab marginal for sustained weeks.
   - Hiring: fast-hire (contractor) recommended for short coverage; 1 FT infra hire only if kicker extends beyond 12 weeks.
   - Decision rule: if kicker persistence forecast > 10 weeks -> immediate commit; otherwise prefer slab + contractor surge.

3) Price compression (-20% slab price)
   - New slab price: $0.000020/token.
   - Tipping point calculator: compare blended cost of continuing smaller commit + slab vs moving full-load to slab.
   - For baseline 120B: full-slab cost = 120B * $0.000020 = $2.4M. Current hybrid = $2.52M -> slab-alone is cheaper by ~$120k/mo.
   - BUT non-monetary costs: SRE burnout, SLA risk, multi-tenant noisy neighbor risk.
   - Proposed NPV-run: prefer slab-only if forecasted slab price stability > 6 months and monitoring + ops overtime budget added. Otherwise keep small commit and monitor.

Switchback rules (operational playbook):
- Entry to commit (scale-up) triggers when 7d sustained forecasted utilization > 85% of slab pool AND expected persistence > 4 weeks.
- Exit (switchback to slab) triggers when 28d rolling average demand drops below 65% of commit capacity AND expected slab price <= 95% of commit effective marginal for >= 8 weeks.
- Soft constraints: automatic alerts to finance and SRE, 72-hour cooling period before irrevocable procurement decisions.

Headcount plan mapping (table-like bullets):
- Baseline posture: 2 infra ops FT, 3 oncall SREs (rotation), 0 immediate new hires.
- Medium commit spin-up: +1 infra ops (contractor immediately, FT hire if >12w), +1 infra engineer for GPU fleet config.
- Large commit adoption: +2 infra ops, +1 capacity program manager, recommend hiring pipeline start (3 months lead).

Sensitivity summary (one-liners):
- Small price moves (±10%): prefer operational levers (batching, KV cache, minor commit adjustments) rather than hiring.
- Demand shocks with short persistence (<8w): slab + contractor surge wins economically.
- Demand shocks >12w: commit ladder yields lower unit cost and protects SLAs; start FT hiring funnel at week 8.
- Rapid slab price deflation sustained >6 months: evaluate slab-only migration with staggered contractual protections and oncall staffing increase.

Open questions / notes-to-self (work-in-progress):
- Need better estimate for slab-induced SRE burnout cost (overtime, retention hit). Add a friction multiplier to slab marginal cost.
- Confirm procurement lead times for reserved pools in new regions (APAC). Current 3w estimate may be optimistic.
- Run Monte Carlo on kicker frequency (historical seasonality + sales pipeline signals).
- Align with Sales on contract language for temporary committed capacity credits if commit spun down within 90d.

Action items (short):
- <@Marco Ruiz> run a 12-month monte carlo with kicker probability buckets and output expected monthly burn under each policy (baseline/hybrid/slab-only).
- <@Ellen Park> validate committed tier pricing with procurement (ask for expedited spin-up lead times).
- Finance: bake in SRE friction multiplier of +12% to slab marginal cost and re-check tipping points.
- Ops: draft automated alert thresholds in observability (7d util, 28d rolling triggers) and link to runbook.

Appendix (quick worked numbers):
- Baseline blended per-token cost (hybrid): total / 120B = $2.52M / 120B = $0.000021.
- Slab-only per-token cost (post-compression): $0.000020.
- Break-even slab price for slab-only at baseline = hybrid total / 120B = $0.000021 i.e. slab needs to be <= $0.000021 to prefer slab-only ignoring non-cost factors.

Revision history:
- 2024-04-12 created initial hypothesis and baseline numbers.
- 2025-09-09 updated commit tier prices after procurement review.
- 2026-02-17 adjusted SRE headcount mapping and added decision windows for switchback policy.

Notes: this is a working proforma, numbers are intentionally simplified for decision clarity. Insert full spreadsheet tabs for per-week cash flows, ramp curves, and hire ramp modeling in the linked proforma workbook.
